objectives: Hear /p/ followed by /l/ at the start of a taught word.
Blend initial /pl/ smoothly without inserting an extra vowel.
Identify words beginning with pl and distinguish them from words beginning with p alone.
Use sound evidence to identify the whole word.
concepts: A consonant blend contains adjacent consonant phonemes that remain audible.
The pl onset contains /p/ followed by /l/.
Smooth blending keeps the consonants close without inserting a vowel.
Listening for /l/ distinguishes pl-words from words beginning with /p/ alone.

definitions.definition: Two adjacent consonant sounds that can both be heard, such as /p/ and /l/ in plan.
The initial consonant sound or group before the vowel.
Joining phonemes closely in order without inserting an extra vowel.

workedExamples.prompt: Say the first two sounds in plan.

workedExamples.solution: Keep /p/ and /l/ close and blend to read plug.

commonMistakes: Skipping /l/ and reading plug as pug.
Guessing from p without checking the next sound.
keyTakeaways: Keep both consonants audible and close together.
Plan, plug, plum, plot and plop begin with pl.
Check the whole word after blending.
revisionPoints: Do not insert a vowel between the consonants.
Contrast plan with pan to hear the difference.

basic.prompt: Name a word that begins with pl.
Which word begins with pl: plum or pan?

conceptual.prompt: Why is pl a consonant blend?
conceptual.answer: Both /p/ and /l/ can be heard in order.

conceptual.prompt: What should you avoid between /p/ and /l/?
How is plum different from pum?
conceptual.answer: Plum has /l/ after /p/; pum does not.

application.prompt: Which word begins with pl and has short /u/?

application.answer: Blend /p/ and /l/ closely to say plop.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: Why listen for /l/ when identifying a pl-word?
higherOrderThinking.answer: It distinguishes pl from words beginning with /p/ alone.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: How can you check a guessed word?
higherOrderThinking.answer: Say each phoneme in order and blend the whole word.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: Which contrast helps hear pl: plan/pan or plan/plug?
higherOrderThinking.answer: plan/pan, because it contrasts pl with /p/ alone.

mixedReview.prompt: What is the onset in plot?
Which word begins with pl and ends in /m/?

mixedReview.answer: An extra vowel between the consonants

activities.name: Hear and blend pl-words.
steps: Say both sounds close together without an extra vowel.
Blend the vowel and final sounds.
Repeat with plan, plug, plum, plot and plop.

activities.name: Contrast pl-words with words beginning with p alone.
steps: Sort plan, plug, plum, pan and pin.
Say the first two sounds in each word.
Read each word to confirm the sort.
